body: This moves platforms *inside* the scene setup, that doesn't sound right, what documentation are you referring to?

> No it doesn't – it happens before scene setup, after `register_scene_singletons()`. Arguably they all should be registered earlier – before/during initialization level core 

Not it happens before the end of the scene initialization, which ends on 3686

I don't see how any of that documentation is an indication that this change is necessary, please explain

Please see https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/53295 for the initialization and encapsulation order, these changes violate this I'd say, and I can't find any other indication that the order changes here match any official order or expected order

> I don't see how any of that documentation is an indication that this change is necessary, please explain

These classes should either be not included on runtime with docs mentioning lack of their presence (instead of pointing out that they are mocked), or be available while initializing the GDExtensions.

> Please see #53295 for the initialization and encapsulation order, these changes violate this I'd say, and I can't find any other indication that the order changes here match any official order or expected order

That's reasonable! Nothing in Engine itself should depend directly on platforms API and proper initialization order ensures that; unfortunately it is not true for GDExtensions :thinking:. 

First of all, thank you for your service!!! 

secondly  – I think it is something that should be discussed during core/gdextension meetings (the next one is on Jan 6). I'll probably push for a suggested workaround (using mainloop startup or another initialization level) instead of changing aforementioned property.

Perhaps this should start with an issue detailing the problem? Because I think the problem is clear, even if the exact solution may not be.

That problem is: GDExtensions can't load methods from platform APIs at _any_ initialization level. So, if a GDExtension binding is designed to load all methods during initialization (the Rust binding has a mode that does this, which makes it a little surprising that we haven't noticed this before) then it can't load methods for this tiny group of classes, and there's nothing in the `extension_api.json` that indicates that these ones are special

> unfortunately it is not true for GDExtensions 

The problem is that this code is not only about GDExtensions, it affects how other parts of the engine functions

But indeed a detailed issue would be useful, this sounds like it might be a problem downstream in extensions not utilizing the API as it is designed or failing to account for it, that might require some clearer documentation to help avoid that

> So, if a GDExtension binding is designed to load all methods during initialization (the Rust binding has a mode that does this, which makes it a little surprising that we haven't noticed this before) then it can't load methods for this tiny group of classes, and there's nothing in the `extension_api.json` that indicates that these ones are special

To explain why godot-rust starts up despite this: platform classes are [special-cased as excluded](https://github.com/godot-rust/gdext/blob/ba379402eb6271c42e860d25b5a4d86890c8fe77/godot-codegen/src/special_cases/special_cases.rs#L140-L150) outside their platform. Android/Wasm builds currently don't have CI coverage, unfortunately.
Closing this PR – the presented solution is definitively not a correct thing to do :tm: and we can continue in proposal/issue.
